summary: A cleaned CSV of all ~6,200 Medicare-enrolled Ambulatory Surgery Centers (ASCs) in the United States, extracted from the CMS Provider of Services (POS) public file and the CMS Facility Characteristics file. Fields include ASC name, address, city, state, ZIP, CMS Certification Number (CCN), Medicare enrollment status, specialty type (general surgery, ophthalmology, GI, orthopedics, etc.), and procedure volume where available. ASCs are the fastest-growing care site in the US — procedure volume has shifted dramatically from hospitals to ASCs, creating a large and active B2B sales market. No affordable standalone CSV exists on Gumroad or any low-cost marketplace. Target buyers are medical device sales reps calling on ASC administrators, pharmaceutical companies targeting ASC-based surgeons, anesthesia billing and staffing firms, and ASC management consulting companies. Priced at $49 one-time.

audience.who: Medical device and surgical supply sales reps building territory call lists for ASC administrators and clinical directors (orthopedic implants, ophthalmology devices, GI scopes, and single-use surgical tools are heavily purchased at the ASC level); pharmaceutical and biologics reps targeting surgeons and anesthesiologists at independent ASCs not covered by hospital GPO contracts; anesthesia staffing and billing companies (USAP, NorthStar Anesthesia) prospecting for new ASC management contracts; ASC consulting and development firms doing greenfield site analysis; and healthcare IT vendors (ASC-specific EHR/PM systems like Surgical Information Systems, AmkaiOffice) doing outbound to independent ASC operators.

data_wanted: CMS Provider of Services (POS) file — hospital and non-hospital facilities extract, filtered to facility type code '17' (Ambulatory Surgery Center). Fields: facility name, CMS Certification Number (CCN/provider number), street address, city, state, ZIP, phone number, Medicare participation status (participating/non-participating), and accreditation body (AAAHC, Joint Commission, AAAASF). Supplemented with CMS Facility Characteristics file for specialty focus (ophthalmology, GI/endoscopy, orthopedics, multi-specialty, etc.) and annual Medicare procedure volume. Both files are freely downloadable from data.cms.gov with no authentication required. Direct download: https://data.cms.gov/provider-characteristics/hospitals-and-other-facilities/provider-of-services-file-hospital-non-hospital-facilities — filter to ASC facility type.

evidence.source: CMS Provider of Services (POS) file — publicly downloadable file of all Medicare-enrolled facilities including ASCs, updated quarterly, no authentication required
evidence.quote: The Provider of Services (POS) file contains information on institutional providers that have filed the Medicare enrollment application (CMS-855A) and have been approved to provide services to Medicare beneficiaries.

evidence.source: ASC Association Fast Facts — 6,200+ Medicare-certified ASCs in the US as of 2024, with procedure volume growing 4% annually as procedures shift from hospitals
evidence.quote: There are approximately 6,200 Medicare-certified ASCs in the United States. ASCs perform more than 23 million procedures annually, with outpatient procedure volumes shifting from hospital settings to ASCs across orthopedics, ophthalmology, GI, and spine surgery.

evidence.source: Becker's ASC Review — trade publication covering the ASC market, confirms active B2B sales interest in ASC contact data for device reps, staffing, and management companies
evidence.quote: The ASC market has attracted major investment from private equity, health systems, and surgical specialty groups. Vendors targeting ASCs — from single-use device makers to EHR vendors — need reliable facility-level contact data to reach independent ASC operators outside hospital GPO structures.

evidence.source: HealthLeaders Media — confirms that medical device companies prioritize ASC sales channels as hospital GPO contracts compress margins, driving demand for ASC-specific prospect lists
evidence.quote: Device companies are redirecting sales resources to ASCs as capitated hospital contracts shrink margins. ASC administrators are often independent decision-makers without GPO constraints — a high-value, high-conversion prospect segment.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Medical device territory reps routinely purchase contact lists of healthcare facilities for their call calendars. Healthcare data brokers (Definitive Healthcare, SK&A) charge $5,000–$15,000/year for ASC-level facility intelligence. A $49 CSV of all 6,200 Medicare-enrolled ASCs — with name, address, ZIP, phone, specialty focus, and Medicare status — delivers the core prospecting data at a one-time price that any individual device rep can expense without manager approval. The healthcare IT and staffing segments (anesthesia, surgical staffing) represent additional buyer cohorts with similar list-buying behavior.
